title: Micro-Lens: Compact Recommendation Strip for Caching & Batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a compact, low-friction recommendation strip (Micro-Lens) to surface targeted caching and batching configuration suggestions directly in the route and model detail headers inside Redwood Console. The goal is to increase adoption of cost-saving best practices without disrupting existing workflows.

Goals:
- Surface high-value, contextual recommendations in 1–2 lines with an expandable explainer.
- Provide safe one-click actions (Apply preset / Preview effect / Schedule rollout) with built-in guardrails and rollback hooks.
- Offer quick, low-cost simulations that estimate latency and token-cost delta before applying.
- Make recommendations explainable (why this change, confidence band, risk note).

Scope and UX notes:
- The Micro-Lens appears in model/route headers and in the route optimization panel. It should not replace the full Config Playground; it's a lightweight nudge.
- Visual design: compact chip + short copy + chevron to expand. When expanded it shows: rationale, expected token delta (range), a micro-sparkline for latency vs throughput, and two actions: Apply Preset / Preview Simulation.
- Presets are context-aware (e.g., small-batch-prefill for chat routes vs large-batch for embeddings). The lens will suggest one preset + 1 conservative alternate.
- Guardrails: recommended max batch size, prefill threshold, and an opt-in canary rollout (5% traffic) with automatic rollback on error rate or latency regression.
- Accessibility: must meet AA contrast, keyboard focus for all actions, and screen-reader friendly labels for the expanded explainer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype (desktop) with expanded/contracted states and inline simulation available.
- Clickable Apply Preset calls an API (spec draft) which returns a dry-run preview.
- Canary rollout flow wired to existing Rollouts UI (schedule & %).
- Unit conversion of token-cost estimates to customer currency via existing cost-service.
- Usability test with 6 engineers/PMs showing >80% comprehension of risk vs reward.
- Instrumentation plan for adoption (clicks), simulation runs, apply events, and rollback events.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Micro-Lens impression -> simulation conversion rate, impression -> apply rate.
- Median token-cost delta for routes where presets applied.
- Canary rollback frequency (should be <2% of canaries in first 30 days).
- NPS/qual feedback from pilot customers.

Design constraints and engineering notes:
- Simulation must run within 5s for the micro-preview. Use sampled trace distributions stored in metrics service and a simplified cost estimator in the Console.
- Avoid making changes that require model re-compilation; prefer config-layer changes (batching, prefill, cache TTL).
- All Apply actions create an audit log entry visible in the route's activity stream.

Open questions:
- Should Micro-Lens be opt-out per route or per org? (PM leaning toward per-route opt-out).
- How to display confidence when telemetry is sparse (new routes)? Proposal: show a ‘low-data’ badge and present conservative suggestions only.
- Should presets be user-editable before Apply? Initial plan: offer ‘Advanced edit’ only in the full Config Playground to keep Micro-Lens quick.

Next steps:
- Finalize copy and variants for low-data / high-confidence states.
- Deliver high-fidelity Figma screens and a clickable prototype.
- Sync with Eng on API dry-run contract and cost estimation endpoint.
- Schedule 1-day moderated usability sessions.

test_plan: Usability: 6 moderated sessions with tasks and SUS scoring. Engineering: end-to-end dry-run + apply in staging with Canary 5% traffic. Monitoring: track impression -> apply conversion, simulation runtime percentile, and canary rollback alerts.
release_notes_blurb: Adds a compact recommendation strip to model and route headers that surfaces contextual batching and caching suggestions. Provides quick previews, one-click presets, and safe canary rollouts with rollback hooks. Pilot release behind a feature flag.
